title: Solar Panel Inspection from Drone Images
summary: Turn drone thermal and RGB surveys of solar plants into a checked defect register mapped to block, inverter, string and module, ready for O&M work orders and warranty evidence.

seo.title: Solar Panel Drone Inspection with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that analyses drone thermography of solar plants, classifies hotspots and module defects, maps them to strings and produces O&M-ready reports.

problem.intro: Utility-scale solar plants commission drone thermography to find hotspots, failed bypass diodes, disconnected strings and broken glass. The flight itself is quick; turning the resulting stack of radiometric images into a defect list a technician can find on the ground is the slow part.

pain_points.title: Manual tagging of every frame
pain_points.detail: Analysts scroll through thermal frames one by one, so reports lag the flight and defects keep costing generation in the meantime.

pain_points.title: Defects not tied to the layout
pain_points.detail: A hotspot marked on an image is of little use if the technician cannot locate the table, string and module position in the field.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent severity grading
pain_points.detail: Different vendors and analysts grade the same anomaly differently, which makes year-on-year comparison and contractor performance hard to judge.

pain_points.title: Weak evidence for warranty claims
pain_points.detail: Module suppliers and EPC contractors ask for clear thermal and visual evidence per module, which is slow to assemble by hand.

solution.overview: We build an analysis pipeline for drone surveys of ground-mounted and large rooftop plants. It takes radiometric thermal and RGB images with flight logs, rejects frames captured outside valid conditions and georeferences the rest onto your plant layout. Models detect and classify anomalies such as single-cell hotspots, bypass diode and substring patterns, whole-module heating, string outages, cracked glass, soiling and shading. Temperature differences are computed against neighbouring modules from the radiometric data. Each anomaly is mapped to block, inverter, string and module position, graded with your severity rules and reviewed by a thermographer where confidence is low. The output is a defect register, an evidence report and work orders.
capabilities: Detects hotspots, bypass diode and substring patterns, module heating and string outages
Flags cracked or broken glass, soiling, bird droppings and vegetation shading from RGB images
Computes temperature difference against neighbouring modules from radiometric data
Maps every anomaly to block, inverter, string, table and module position
Compares surveys over time to show new, persisting and repaired defects
Cross-checks string outages against string current data from the monitoring system

workflow.title: Upload the survey
workflow.detail: The drone team uploads thermal and RGB images with flight logs, and irradiance and ambient readings come from the plant weather station.

workflow.title: Check capture conditions
workflow.detail: Frames taken at low irradiance, steep angles or with motion blur are flagged for re-flight instead of being analysed.

workflow.title: Detect and classify anomalies
workflow.detail: Models find and classify anomalies and compute temperature differences from the radiometric data.

workflow.title: Map to the plant layout
workflow.detail: Georeferencing places each anomaly on the block, inverter, string and module layout from your as-built drawings.

workflow.title: Thermographer review
workflow.detail: Low-confidence classifications and high-severity findings are reviewed by a qualified thermographer or O&M engineer.

workflow.title: Issue register and work orders
workflow.detail: The approved defect register, evidence report and work orders go to the O&M team and the CMMS.

inputs: Radiometric thermal images from the drone survey
RGB images of the same blocks
Irradiance and ambient temperature from the plant weather station
As-built layout with string and module mapping
outputs: Defect register by block, inverter, string and module
Annotated thermal and RGB evidence per defect
Survey report for O&M and asset management
Survey-over-survey comparison of new and repaired defects
human_in_the_loop: A qualified thermographer or O&M engineer reviews low-confidence and high-severity anomalies and signs off the report. Decisions on module replacement, cleaning and warranty claims stay with your team.
integrations: Drone data platform or cloud storage used by your survey vendor
SCADA or plant monitoring portal for string currents
GIS or CAD exports of the plant layout
Evidence export for module supplier and EPC warranty claims
guardrails: Frames outside valid capture conditions are rejected, not reported as defects
Every defect links to its source images and coordinates
Severity rules are versioned and agreed with the O&M team
Reports are signed off by a named engineer
Plant layout and generation data kept in your cloud account
compliance_notes: Report structure can follow the PV thermography practice your O&M or EPC contract specifies, such as IEC TS 62446-3.
Flights are planned and flown by your licensed drone operator under applicable drone rules; we work only with the resulting data.

pilot.scope: One block of an operating plant, using an existing survey dataset plus one new flight flown to agreed capture parameters.
deliverables: Capture specification for your drone vendor
Processed defect register for the pilot block
Plan and cost for plant-wide and repeat surveys

Time from data upload to signed-off report, compared with the current process.

faqs.a: No. We work with data from your in-house team or survey vendor, and we provide a capture specification covering altitude, overlap, time of day and minimum irradiance so the images are usable for analysis.

faqs.q: Which cameras and file formats do you support?
faqs.a: Radiometric thermal formats from common drone payloads, such as radiometric JPEG or TIFF, plus standard RGB images and flight logs. We confirm compatibility with a sample from your vendor before the pilot.

faqs.q: Can the output support warranty claims?
faqs.a: It assembles the evidence suppliers usually ask for: thermal and RGB images per module, temperature difference, location and survey date. Whether a claim is valid under the warranty terms is decided by your team and the supplier.

faqs.q: Does it work for rooftop and C&I plants?
faqs.a: Yes, where the drone can capture usable angles and layout drawings exist. Rooftop surveys often need more manual layout mapping, which we scope during the pilot.
